chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مَسْعُودٍ، عَنْ أَبِي عَلِيٍّ الْمَحْمُودِيِّ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَحْمَدَ بْنِ حَمَّادٍ الْمَرْوَزِيِّ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Mas'ud, from Abu Ali al-Mahmudi Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Hammad al-Marwazi who said:

chunks.arabic_text: كَتَبَ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ إِلَى أَبِي فِي فَصْلٍ مِنْ كِتَابِهِ، فَكَانَ تَوَفِّيَ مِنْ يَوْمٍ أَوْ غَدٍ

translations.en: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) wrote to my father in a part of his letter, and he (my father) died on the same day or the next.

chunks.arabic_text: ثُمَّ وَفِّيَتْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَا كَسَبَتْ وَهُمْ لَا يُظْلَمُونَ

translations.en: Then 'every soul will be recompensed for that which it earned and they will not be dealt with unjustly'.

chunks.arabic_text: أَمَّا الدُّنْيَا فَنَحْنُ فِيهَا مُتَفَرِّجُونَ فِي الْبِلَادِ وَلَكِنْ مَنْ هَوَى هَوَى صَاحِبِهِ وَدَانَ بِدِينِهِ فَهُوَ مَعَهُ وَإِنْ كَانَ نَائِيًا عَنْهُ

translations.en: As for this world, then we are in it separated in different lands, but whoever inclines to the inclination of his fellow (Imam) and takes as a religion his [fellow’s] religion, then he is with him even if he is [geographically] distant from him.
And as for the next world, then 'it is the everlasting abode'.

en.summary: This letter from Imam al-Jawad (AS) to Ahmad ibn Hammad clarifies the distinction between worldly separation and spiritual unity, emphasizing that shared adherence to the Imam's guidance binds believers despite geographical distance. It contrasts the transient, observational nature of this life with the eternal, permanent abode of the Hereafter, reinforcing the Shia concept of *Tawalla* (affiliation) as the true determinant of spiritual proximity. The reference to 'each soul earning what it has earned' underscores individual accountability within the framework of Imamate.
en.seo_question: How does the Imam explain spiritual unity in the world versus physical unity in the afterlife?
